summary: Kameshwar Nath Mishra worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying under Ram Chandra Dwivedi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–1988, 2001) and was a visiting research scholar at the University of Marburg (1993).

Kamil Václav Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Prague (1946–1952). He held posts at the Oriental Institute (1952–1970), University of Prague (~1960–1968), and Utrecht University (~1977–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry studied at Santiniketan (~1938–1940), University of the Punjab, University of Calcutta (~1943–1945), and Michigan State University (~1947–1949). She later held posts at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi worked in Indology and religious studies after studying under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of Kalidasa Akademi, and Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Mount Holyoke College (~1996–2000) and completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (~2001–2009) under David F. Germano and Paul Groner. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Having studied under Su Bai, he serves as dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, studying under Sukumar Sengupta and earning a PhD at the University of Ceylon (~1965–1968) under Sirima Kiribamune. He was appointed Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta around 1968.
Kanchu Onoue was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as an instructor at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).
Kang Youwei was a Chinese philosopher and sinologist. In 1890, he founded the Wanmu Caotang, where he held a post from around 1891 to 1898 and taught Qichao Liang.

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yün-hua Jan (attested 1976). He later held a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary (attested 1999) under Anthony W. Barber and also studied under Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, attended the University of Paris (~1928–1931), and held an appointment at the Tokyo Imperial Household Museum (~1932–1948).

Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962). He served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).
Kanti Chandra Pandey worked in Indology and philosophy. He founded the University of Lucknow, where he also held a post (attested 1950).

Kapila Vatsyayan was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who earned degrees from Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, served as chairperson of India International Centre (~1993–2020), and held multiple leadership roles at IGNCA (1987–2005).

Karel Werner worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning his doctorate at Palacký University (~1945–1949). He held posts at Palacký University (~1947–1964), Durham University (1969–1990), Masaryk University (1993–1998), and was an honorary research associate at SOAS (1993).

Karen Cheatham is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree from the Graduate Theological Union and a doctoral degree from the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Karen Christina Lang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg (-1983). She served as professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1991–2019).

Karen McCarthy Brown was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University (1970–1976). She served as professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976–2009) alongside appointments at Temple, Barnard, Harvard, and other institutions.
